home_care: Withhold food for 12-24h (water still available), then reintroduce a bland diet (boiled chicken and rice) in small portions.
vet_if: Symptoms last beyond 24-48h, blood appears, or the dog is a puppy, senior, or has other health conditions.
diet_notes: Bland, low-fat food during recovery; gradual transition back to normal diet over 3-4 days.

home_care: This is a medical emergency, especially in unvaccinated puppies - do not attempt home treatment.
vet_if: Immediately - parvovirus is life-threatening and requires hospitalization and IV fluids.
diet_notes: Diet is managed by the vet during recovery; bland, easily digestible food is reintroduced gradually once vomiting stops.

home_care: Use a harness instead of a collar, rest in a humid room, and isolate from other dogs to prevent spread.
vet_if: Cough persists over a week, worsens, or is paired with fever/lethargy/appetite loss.
diet_notes: No special diet needed; ensure easy access to water and soft food if throat irritation reduces appetite.

home_care: Keep ears dry, avoid inserting cotton swabs into the canal, and check for foreign debris.
vet_if: Symptoms persist beyond a few days, there's a strong odor/discharge, or the dog shows head tilt or balance issues.
diet_notes: If allergy-related, an elimination diet trial (limited-ingredient or novel-protein food) may help identify triggers.

home_care: Regular bathing with a gentle/hypoallergenic shampoo and reducing exposure to known irritants.
vet_if: Itching is constant, skin becomes broken/infected, or there's no improvement with basic care.
diet_notes: Limited-ingredient or hydrolyzed-protein diet trial can help rule out food allergies as a cause.

home_care: Use a vet-approved flea preventative and treat the home environment (bedding, carpets) for fleas.
vet_if: Skin is broken or infected, or the itching persists despite flea control.
diet_notes: No specific diet link; ensure overall coat/skin health with adequate omega-3 fatty acid intake.

home_care: Encourage water intake to dilute urine; do not delay care if straining is present.
vet_if: Straining with little/no urine output (possible blockage - urgent), or blood in urine.
diet_notes: Urinary-support diets (controlled mineral content) may be recommended long-term if UTIs recur.

home_care: None - this is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate veterinary surgery.
vet_if: Immediately, this cannot wait - bloat can be fatal within hours.
diet_notes: Prevention: feed smaller, multiple meals rather than one large meal, and avoid vigorous exercise right after eating.

home_care: Provide soft bedding, moderate low-impact exercise, and weight management to reduce joint stress.
vet_if: Pain worsens, mobility declines quickly, or over-the-counter relief isn't helping (never give human painkillers).
diet_notes: Joint-support diets with glucosamine/chondroitin and omega-3s; keep weight in the ideal range to reduce joint load.

home_care: Not manageable at home alone; requires diagnosis and lifelong medication from a vet.
vet_if: Persistent unexplained weight gain, lethargy, or coat changes.
diet_notes: Calorie-controlled diet to manage weight gain, alongside prescribed thyroid medication.

home_care: Not manageable without veterinary diagnosis; requires blood glucose monitoring and likely insulin.
vet_if: Any combination of increased thirst/urination with weight loss despite normal or increased appetite.
diet_notes: Consistent, high-fiber, controlled-carbohydrate diet fed on a fixed schedule aligned with insulin dosing.

home_care: Ensure constant access to fresh water; avoid high-sodium treats.
vet_if: Persistent increased thirst/urination, weight loss, or appetite decline in middle-aged/senior dogs.
diet_notes: Prescription renal diet: reduced phosphorus and controlled, high-quality protein.

home_care: Withhold fatty foods and table scraps immediately; do not attempt to treat without vet guidance.
vet_if: Vomiting combined with abdominal pain and hunched posture, especially after a fatty meal.
diet_notes: Low-fat prescription diet during and after recovery; strictly avoid fatty table scraps long-term.

home_care: Restrict exercise if diagnosed - exertion increases risk of complications during treatment.
vet_if: Persistent cough with reduced stamina, especially if heartworm prevention has lapsed.
diet_notes: No special diet; focus is on monthly preventatives and following the vet's treatment/exercise-restriction plan.

home_care: Gently wipe discharge with a clean, damp cloth; prevent scratching with an e-collar if needed.
vet_if: Discharge is thick/colored, symptoms persist beyond a couple days, or the eye looks cloudy/painful.
diet_notes: No specific diet link.

home_care: Regular tooth brushing and dental chews; avoid very hard chew toys that can crack teeth.
vet_if: Bad breath with visible tartar/red gums, or difficulty eating - professional cleaning may be needed.
diet_notes: Dental-formula kibble can help reduce plaque buildup; softer food temporarily if eating is painful.

home_care: Gradually increase exercise and portion-control meals; avoid free-feeding.
vet_if: To rule out underlying causes (thyroid, etc.) and get a tailored weight-loss plan.
diet_notes: Calorie-controlled, high-fiber/high-protein weight-management food; measured portions, minimal treats.

home_care: Check for and safely remove attached ticks; use vet-recommended tick prevention.
vet_if: Shifting limb lameness with fever, especially after known tick exposure.
diet_notes: No special diet; focus on preventative tick control.

home_care: Low-impact exercise (swimming), soft bedding, and ramps instead of stairs.
vet_if: Progressive difficulty rising or walking, particularly in large-breed dogs.
diet_notes: Weight management is critical; joint-support diet with glucosamine/chondroitin.

home_care: Vet or groomer can manually express the glands; avoid attempting this without guidance.
vet_if: Recurrent scooting, swelling, or discharge/bleeding near the tail base.
diet_notes: Higher-fiber diet can help produce firmer stools that naturally express the glands.

home_care: Wipe discharge gently, use a humidifier, and warm up food slightly to make it more appealing.
vet_if: Symptoms persist beyond a week, breathing becomes labored, or the cat stops eating entirely.
diet_notes: Warmed, aromatic wet food can encourage eating when smell/appetite is reduced by congestion.

home_care: Encourage water intake, provide clean litter boxes, and reduce stress in the home.
vet_if: Straining with little/no urine (urgent - possible blockage, especially in male cats) or visible blood.
diet_notes: Urinary-support wet food (higher moisture, controlled mineral content) to promote dilute urine.

home_care: Not manageable at home alone; requires blood testing and ongoing treatment (medication, diet, or other therapy).
vet_if: Weight loss despite a ravenous appetite, especially in middle-aged to senior cats.
diet_notes: Prescription iodine-restricted diet is one treatment option, alongside or instead of medication.

home_care: Provide multiple fresh water sources; consider wet food to increase hydration.
vet_if: Increased thirst/urination with weight loss, common in senior cats.
diet_notes: Prescription renal diet: reduced phosphorus, controlled high-quality protein, high moisture content.

home_care: Not manageable without vet diagnosis; requires monitoring and typically insulin.
vet_if: Increased thirst/urination with weight loss, especially in overweight or older cats.
diet_notes: High-protein, low-carbohydrate diet fed consistently, aligned with insulin schedule if prescribed.

home_care: Regular brushing to reduce loose fur ingestion; hairball-control treats in moderation.
vet_if: Frequent vomiting, or retching without producing a hairball (possible blockage).
diet_notes: Hairball-control formula food (added fiber) helps fur pass through the digestive tract naturally.

home_care: This is a medical emergency, especially in unvaccinated kittens - do not attempt home treatment.
vet_if: Immediately - this is often fatal without prompt veterinary care.
diet_notes: Diet is managed by the vet during recovery; bland food reintroduced gradually once stable.

home_care: Keep ears clean; avoid sharing bedding between pets until treated to prevent spread.
vet_if: Persistent scratching with dark, coffee-ground-like debris in the ears.
diet_notes: No specific diet link.

home_care: Use a vet-approved flea preventative and treat the home environment for fleas.
vet_if: Skin becomes broken/infected or itching persists despite flea control.
diet_notes: No specific diet link; adequate omega-3 intake supports skin/coat health.

home_care: Tooth brushing if tolerated, and dental-formula treats; monitor eating for signs of pain.
vet_if: Bad breath with visible red/inflamed gums, or reluctance to eat.
diet_notes: Softer wet food temporarily if chewing is painful; dental kibble for long-term plaque control.

home_care: Increase water intake (wet food, water fountains) and ensure adequate exercise.
vet_if: No stool for 48+ hours, or repeated straining without result.
diet_notes: High-fiber or wet food to soften stool; ensure good hydration overall.

home_care: Reduce airborne irritants (smoke, dust, strong sprays) in the home.
vet_if: Any breathing difficulty is urgent - open-mouth breathing in cats is always a red flag.
diet_notes: Weight management if overweight, as excess weight worsens respiratory strain.

home_care: Gently wipe discharge with a clean, damp cloth; prevent scratching with an e-collar if needed.
vet_if: Discharge is thick/colored, persists beyond a couple days, or the eye looks cloudy/painful.
diet_notes: No specific diet link.

home_care: Portion-controlled meals, interactive play/toys, and avoiding free-feeding.
vet_if: To rule out underlying causes and get a tailored weight-loss plan.
diet_notes: Calorie-controlled, high-protein weight-management food; measured portions, minimal treats.

home_care: Not manageable at home alone; requires vet diagnosis to rule out other causes first.
vet_if: Vomiting or diarrhea that is recurring/chronic rather than a one-off episode.
diet_notes: Novel-protein or hydrolyzed-protein prescription diet is often part of long-term management.

home_care: Isolate from other pets/people (it's contagious) and disinfect shared surfaces/bedding.
vet_if: Any suspected ringworm, since it's zoonotic (can spread to humans) and needs confirmed diagnosis.
diet_notes: No specific diet link; general skin/coat-supporting nutrition (omega-3s) can aid recovery.

home_care: Keep as an indoor-only cat to reduce exposure to infections and prevent spreading to other cats.
vet_if: Recurring infections or unexplained weight loss - testing is needed for diagnosis.
diet_notes: High-quality, easily digestible diet to support a compromised immune system; avoid raw food due to infection risk.

home_care: Keep as an indoor-only cat to prevent spreading the virus to other cats.
vet_if: Any of these symptoms in combination - testing is needed for diagnosis and management planning.
diet_notes: High-quality, easily digestible diet to support a compromised immune system; avoid raw food due to infection risk.

home_care: Do not withhold food for long periods in cats (unlike dogs) - prolonged fasting can be harmful; consult a vet.
vet_if: Appetite loss lasting more than a day, especially with vomiting or lethargy.
diet_notes: Low-fat, easily digestible prescription diet; small frequent meals during recovery.

home_care: Reduce environmental stressors, provide multiple litter boxes, and enrich the home environment.
vet_if: To rule out infection/blockage first, since symptoms overlap with FLUTD/UTI.
diet_notes: Wet food to increase water intake; consistent routine and feeding schedule to reduce stress.
